Since 28 February 2026, the United States and  Israel have been at war with Iran and its regional allies. Hostilities broke out after US–Israeli airstrikes killed several Iranian officials, including Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei. The strikes were launched amid ongoing US–Iran negotiations regarding Iran's nuclear program.

The war is part of a Middle Eastern crisis sparked by the Gaza war. It follows the Twelve-Day War and was preceded by the largest US military buildup in the region since the 2003 invasion of Iraq. US justifications for initiating the war included a response to the crackdown on anti-government protests in Iran, preventing Iran from obtaining a nuclear weapon, regime change, and taking Iran's oil and gas resources. Critics have rejected these justifications, maintaining that the attack initiated a war of aggression, in violation of international law.

Following a decentralized strategy, Iranian units responded with a series of missile and drone attacks against Israel, US-aligned Arab countries, and US military bases across the region, and by blocking the Strait of Hormuz in late March. Following the strikes on their territory, the United Arab Emirates, Saudi Arabia, and Kuwait also attacked Iran and skirmished with its Iraqi non-state allies.  Two days after Khamenei's assassination, fighting resumed between Hezbollah and Israel. Israel began occupying southern Lebanon in March. The war has resulted in thousands of civilian and military casualties. The economic impact of the war included the largest ever supply disruption of the global oil market, disruptions of the natural gas, fertilizer, aviation, and tourism industries, and volatility in financial markets. As of June 2026[update], the cost of the war to the US was estimated at $113.3 billion,[73][74] while the Trump administration asked for $1.5 trillion for the Pentagon over the next fiscal year, setting a record in modern US military spending.[75]

The secretary-general of the United Nations and several countries condemned the US–Israeli strikes, while the United Nations Security Council passed a resolution condemning Iran's retaliatory strikes on Gulf states. A two-week ceasefire beginning on 8 April came under strain after Iran responded to Israeli attacks on Lebanon by resuming its blockade.[76] After the failure of the Islamabad Talks on 12–13 April, the US imposed its own naval blockade. A memorandum to end the war was signed on 17 June by the presidents of the US and Iran, lifting the dual blockade. Tensions again escalated, but on 28 June, the US and Iran agreed to cease their exchange of attacks. On 8 July, the ceasefire deal between the US and Iran collapsed after attacks by both sides.

The initial strikes on Iran were codenamed Operation Epic Fury by the United States government,[77][78][79] and Operation Roaring Lion[y] by the Israeli government,[80][81] in line with their codename of Operation Rising Lion for their strikes on Iran during the Twelve-Day War in June 2025. The war has also been referred to by some outlets as the "Third Gulf War" (Gulf War III), following the Gulf War (1990–1991), and the Iraq War (2003–2011), which has also been referred to as the "Second Gulf War" (Gulf War II).[ab] Iranian state media has referred to the conflict as the "Third Imposed War",[89][90] with the Iran–Iraq War (1980–1988) and the Twelve-Day War respectively as the "First" and "Second".[91][92] Due to the war starting during the month of Ramadan, it has sometimes been called the "Ramadan War".[ac][ad]

A US- and UK-backed coup d'état in 1953 deposed the democratically-elected Iranian prime minister Mohammad Mosaddegh due to his nationalization of the oil industry, strengthening the rule of Shah Mohammad Reza Pahlavi. Israel maintained ties with Iran as part of its alliance of the periphery strategy. Resentment of the Shah's autocratic rule led to the 1979 revolution in which Pahlavi was overthrown and replaced by an Islamic republic.[98][99] Iran severed diplomatic ties with the US and Israel and held the American embassy staff hostage,[100] releasing them after signing the Algiers Accords (1981), in which, among other things, the US agreed not to intervene in Iranian affairs anymore.[101]

During the Iran–Iraq War, the US supported Iraq. In 1988, a US warship struck an Iranian mine, and the US responded by attacking Iran's navy. A few months later, the US mistakenly shot down a civilian Iranian flight.[102][103] Iran started a ballistic missile program to deter Iraqi missile attacks on Iranian cities during the 1980–88 Iran–Iraq War and to compensate for its lack of a modern air force due to sanctions.[104]

Starting in the 1985, Iran began engaging in proxy conflicts throughout the Middle East.[105] These proxy groups became part of the informal 'Axis of Resistance' committed primarily to countering American, Israeli, Saudi, Emirati, and sometimes Turkish influence in the region.[106][107][108][109][110]

In 2002, Iran's covert nuclear program was first revealed, and Iran denied seeking a weapon. In 2003, Iran's AMAD Project was suspended following Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei's fatwa against nuclear weapons.[111][112] In 2005, the US began imposing sanctions targeting Iran's nuclear program, and in 2006 the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) imposed a series of sanctions against Iran. The US and Israel conducted a campaign of cyberwarfare against Iranian nuclear facilities to disrupt their operations, while Israel assassinated several top Iranian nuclear scientists.[103][113] The UNSC concerns about Iran's nuclear program from 2006[ae] led to the multilateral Joint Comprehensive Plan of Action (JCPOA) between Iran and the P5+1 and the EU in 2015.[117]

In January 2020, US president Donald Trump ordered the assassination of Qasem Soleimani, the commander of the Iranian Quds Force.[100][102] Following the October 7 attacks on Israel and the start of the Gaza war, tensions further escalated with Israel fighting Iran-backed militias across the Middle East, including Hamas,[af] Hezbollah, and the Houthis. Israeli strikes on the Iranian consulate in Damascus and the assassinations of Ismail Haniyeh and Hassan Nasrallah in 2024 were met with Iranian strikes on Israel in April and October.[120] In June 2025, Israel launched the Twelve-Day War by attacking Iranian military and nuclear facilities, provoking Iranian counter-strikes. The United States also struck Iranian nuclear facilities during the Twelve-Day War, which ended in a ceasefire.[121]

In early 2026, Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu lobbied President Donald Trump for a joint military strike on Iran, specifically targeting its leadership.[122] Following high-level meetings in February, Trump authorized "Operation Epic Fury", with reports citing Israeli intelligence provided by Netanyahu as a decisive factor in the decision.[123]

Nuclear enrichment has been considered a component of Iranian national development plans since the Shah's regime, when the first nuclear program was developed.[124] Iran retained its nuclear program after the 1979 revolution, and has long denied seeking nuclear weapons, saying its enrichment efforts were to generate nuclear power for civilian use.[125] Despite Iran's compliance with the JCPOA, Trump withdrew the US from the deal in 2018,[126]  re-imposed sanctions, and adopted a "maximum pressure" strategy.[127] The Biden administration kept most of these sanctions, further damaging Iran's economy.[128] Trump continued the "maximum pressure" approach in his second term.[129] In September 2025, the UN reimposed sanctions on Iran using the "snapback" mechanism, causing the currency to weaken, resulting in price increases for food supplies such as meat, rice, and other staples, freezing Iranian assets abroad, suspending arms transactions, and imposing penalties related to the country's ballistic-missile programme.[130][131] Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent labelled the collapse of the Iranian currency in December 2025 as the strategy's "grand culmination".[132][133] At his State of the Union Address in February 2026, Trump claimed Iran had restarted its nuclear program and was developing missiles capable of striking the US.[134] Trump's claims contradicted his previous claims that Iran's nuclear program was "obliterated" and US intelligence reports that Iran did not pose any threat towards the US, and needed until 2035 to build such missiles to do so.[135]

On 12 June 2025, the International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) found Iran non-compliant with its NPT safeguards agreement for the first time since 2005.[136][137] A few days later, it was reported that Iran had stored highly enriched uranium in an underground facility that was undamaged by US bombings in 2025.[138] Subsequently, Iran denied the IAEA access to nuclear facilities that had been bombed, but did provide access to all unaffected facilities.[139] Mohammad Eslami, the head of the Atomic Energy Organization of Iran, said Iran would not permit inspections of facilities struck by the US until the IAEA established rules for the post-war situation, insisting on codified protocols for internationally protected facilities subjected to military attacks, and that the IAEA condemn the attacks.[140]

In February 2026, Iran informed the IAEA that normal safeguards were "legally untenable and materially impracticable," as a result of threats and "acts of aggression," leaving the IAEA unable to verify whether Iran had suspended enrichment or confirm the status of its stockpile,[139] though it found no evidence Iran was weaponizing.[141] Analysts in the UK and US characterized Iran's strategy as nuclear hedging.[142] The Bulletin of the Atomic Scientists said that Iran was using its enrichment program and uranium stockpiles for leverage in international negotiations, and was willing to dilute or export its higher-level enriched uranium in exchange for sanctions relief and prevention of attacks.[143]

Israel is widely believed to possess nuclear weapons, with a stockpile estimated between 90 and 400 nuclear warheads.[154] Israel is the only nuclear-armed country that does not officially acknowledge its nuclear weapons capability.[155] Some scholars have argued that Israel's nuclear weapons have incentivized Iran to develop its own nuclear program, seen as maintaining a balance of nuclear deterrence, or causing a regional nuclear arms race.[156][157][158][159] Citing security threats, Israel rejects international calls to accede to the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons or to participate in negotiations of a Middle East nuclear weapon free zone.[160][161][162] This has frustrated both US[155] and UK[163] diplomatic efforts on such a zone. Scholars also suggest US tacit acceptance of the Israeli nuclear weapons capability is seen as a double standard that undermines its diplomatic credibility in Middle East nonproliferation negotiations.[164][155]

Tension between Iran and the United States during negotiations over Iran's nuclear program intensified in January 2026 when Iranian security forces massacred anti-government protesters.

The US began its greatest buildup of military assets in the region since the Iraq War in 2003. The US accused Iran of building up its nuclear and missile programs to threaten the United States and its allies. Iran accused the US of disinformation. Gulf states like Qatar predicted that escalations could severely harm the region. Negotiations regarding the Iranian nuclear program were held in February until the US and Israel commenced military strikes in Iran on 28 February 2026.

On 27 February at 3:38 p.m. EST (11:08 p.m. IRST), Trump, traveling on Air Force One to Texas, authorized Operation Epic Fury.[77][78] US missiles, drones, and Israeli fighter jets began striking Iran the next day, around 9:45 a.m. IRST (1:15 a.m. EST).[165][166] The strikes took place during negotiations over Iran's nuclear program,[167][168] and coincided with the holy month of Ramadan.[169] The operation was codenamed Operation Roaring Lion[ag] by Israel.[80][81] The Israeli Air Force (IAF) said it struck 500 military targets in Iran in the largest combat sortie in its history.[170] Iranian naval vessels were also targeted.[171] Israel said it used over 1,200 bombs in 24 hours.[172] US strikes were carried out by planes based around the Middle East and from aircraft carriers.[173]

Initial strikes killed Iran's supreme leader Ali Khamenei and other top Iranian officials,[174] and hundreds of Iranians were killed or injured. The Iranian Red Crescent said 24 provinces were affected.[175] The strikes were coupled with cyberattacks on Iranian infrastructure, media, and phone apps, with messages calling on Iranians to rise up against their government.[176][177][178] The cyberattacks resulted in a near-total internet blackout in Iran, lasting over 60 hours with connectivity dropping to as low as 1% of normal levels, disrupting government communications, state media, and public services.[179][177] Iran restricted internet access, allowing access only to government-approved users until 26 May.[180]

Israeli officials said months-long planning preceded the strikes, allowing them to pinpoint targets, attain "tactical surprise", and gain US support.[181] Attacking during the morning, rather than at night when most of Israel's previous attacks on Iran took place, added to the element of surprise.[182] Israel declared a state of emergency, citing expectation of Iranian retaliation, and warned its citizens to remain in protected areas.[183][184] Israel called up 20,000 reservists in addition to the 50,000 on duty.[185] The Israeli Ministry of Health moved its hospital operations underground.[186]

On 28 February, Trump released a statement saying the purpose of the strikes was regime change, citing Iran's support for non-state actors such as Hamas and Hezbollah, killings of protesters, chants of "Death to America", and alleged history of attacking US civilians and soldiers, as well as the Iran hostage crisis.[187] Trump and Benjamin Netanyahu warned of the potential threat of nuclear weapons in Iran and called on Iranians to overthrow their government.[187][188] Israeli defense minister Israel Katz labeled the strikes a "pre-emptive attack" intended to "remove threats to...Israel".[183] Iran denied that it intended to attack the US.[189]

Iranian units reacted within hours by launching missiles and drones. Iran codenamed its response Operation True Promise IV,[ah][ai] and state media dubbed the events the Ramadan War.[aj][95] Iran struck Israeli targets in Tel Aviv and Haifa[190] as well as countries throughout the Persian Gulf.[191] Targets included Bahrain's capital Manama,[192][193] Kuwait International Airport, the United Arab Emirates' capital Abu Dhabi,[194][195] Riyadh and Eastern Province in Saudi Arabia,[196] and Erbil International Airport and the US Consulate General in Erbil in Iraq.[197]

Among the first targets were radars, notably the American AN/FPS-132 in Qatar, which degraded missile-warning capability in the region.[198] Iran reported striking the US bases of Al Udeid Air Base in Qatar, Ali Al Salem Air Base in Kuwait,[199] Al Dhafra Air Base in the UAE, and the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain.[200]  On 1 or 2 March, Iran struck the radar bases for US THAAD missile defense systems in Jordan, the UAE and Saudi Arabia, destroying at least one.[201] On 1 March, Iran launched more strikes,[202] including missiles and drones on Bahrain, Israel, Jordan, Kuwait, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, and the UAE.[203][204] The UK reported "missiles fired in the direction of Cyprus", but "don't believe they were targeted at Cyprus". However, the presidents of Cyprus and Northern Cyprus contradicted the claims that any missiles were fired at Cyprus.[205][206][207]  The Palau-flagged Skylight and Marshall Islands-flagged MKD VYOM tankers were targeted off Oman's coast.[208][209][210] Shipping through the Strait of Hormuz slowed to a standstill,[211] with 150 freight ships, including oil tankers, stalled.[212]

British prime minister Keir Starmer said the US could use British bases for "defensive" strikes on Iran[213] and disclosed that Ukrainian and other specialists would aid Gulf efforts to foil Iranian drone strikes.[214] Saudi Crown Prince Salman, with US backing, vowed to employ military force against Iranian incursions, calling Iranian strikes "cowardly" due to Saudi airspace being closed to US and Israeli attackers.[215] Trump announced that the US had accepted an Iranian proposal to negotiations.[216] However, Ali Larijani ruled out talks.[217]

On 2 March, the US embassy in Kuwait was struck and closed indefinitely.[218][219] The US-flagged tanker Stena Imperative and the Honduras-flagged tanker Athe Nova were struck.[220] An advisor to an IRGC commander said he would set fire to any ship coming through the Strait of Hormuz, and added that no oil will leave the area.[221]

Qatar claimed that it had shot down two Iranian Su-24 bombers.[222] The Qatari Ministry of Defense announced that Ras Laffan Industrial City, the main Qatari gas facility, and Mesaieed Industrial Area were struck by Iranian drones.[223] According to satellite imagery analysis by the Energy Economics and Society Research Institute, Ras Laffan appeared to not have been damaged before the "unprecedented shutdown" which sent fuel prices higher.[224]

The US and Israel attacked the Natanz Nuclear Facility[225] and the Iranian media reported damage to the Khatam-al-Anbia and Gandhi hospitals.[226] In a friendly fire incident, the pilot of an F/A-18 of the Kuwait Air Force shot down three US F-15E fighters.[227][228][229][219] Israel and Hezbollah exchanged strikes.[230] Hezbollah began firing rockets and missiles on Israel in retaliation for the killing of Khamenei.[231] Hezbollah claimed that the attack was a "defensive act" after more than a year of Israeli attacks despite a 2024 truce.[232] It added that it restarted fighting to force Israel to stop its aggression and evacuate from seized Lebanese territories, emphasizing that the move was unrelated to the war.[233]

Lebanon banned military activities by Hezbollah after the attacks.[234] An IDF spokesperson stated the attack was "an official declaration of war by Hezbollah", vowing to "neutralize" the threat.[230] Israel struck southern Lebanon,[235][236][237] Beirut, and the Beqaa Valley,[230] with the IDF saying it had killed the head of Hezbollah's intelligence Hussein Makled[238][239] and Adham Adnan al-Othman, the head of Palestinian Islamic Jihad's armed wing, the Al-Quds Brigades.[240] The Royal Air Force station at Akrotiri, Cyprus, was targeted by a drone strike causing damage to a runway.[241][242][243][244] Another strike on Cyprus led to Greece announcing that it would deploy frigates and F-16s to defend Cyprus from strikes by Iran.[245] The pro-Iran militant group Iraqi Guardians of Blood Brigades claimed responsibility for attacks on the US Victory Base near Baghdad International Airport and Erbil in the Kurdistan Region of Iraq.[246][247][248] The Islamic Resistance in Iraq claimed responsibility for 23 drone strikes on US assets in Erbil.[249]

On 3 March, US and Israeli strikes destroyed the SNSC headquarters,[250] the Expediency Discernment Council building in Tehran,[251] and what Israeli officials described as an alleged underground nuclear weapons facility called Min Zadai.[252] The proximity of these strikes to the Bushehr Nuclear Power Plant (about 12 km (7.5 mi) away) prompted the Russian agency Rosatom to suspend construction on new units and evacuate non-essential staff.[253] A CIA site in US embassy in Riyadh was hit by Iranian drones.[254] US officials said its forces had severely damaged Iran's naval capabilities, mainly in the Gulf of Oman, where several Iranian warships were destroyed and key bases hit.[255][256] Debris from an airstrike damaged Golestan Palace, a UNESCO World Heritage Site,[257] causing UNESCO to issue a statement that damaging UNESCO sites is against international law.[258] Israel Katz authorized a ground invasion of Lebanon on 3 March with forces from the 91st Division, with the stated goal to establish a "security layer" against Hezbollah. The Lebanese government reported that Israeli attacks reached Kfarkela and Qouzah, leading the Lebanese army to redeploy from newly established border posts.[259] Israel reported that it killed Daoud Alizadeh, the commander of the Quds Force's Lebanon branch, in Tehran.[260]

Western diplomats said Qatar had struck Iran after Iran had attempted to strike Doha's airport and Qatar shot down two Iranian Su-24 bombers.[261][262] Qatar denied the accusation that it had joined the "campaign targeting Iran".[263] Iran warned it would hit all economic hubs in the Middle East,[264][265] and any defensive European military involvement would be considered an act of war.[266][267]

On 4 March, US secretary of state Marco Rubio announced that the US-Israeli attacks on Iran would increase in intensity.[268] Israel attacks hit the Basij headquarters.[269] The IDF announced that an F-35I "Adir" shot down a Russian-made Iranian Yak-130 fighter jet over Tehran, the first time that an F-35 has shot down a crewed fighter jet in air-to-air combat, and the first time the IAF shot down an aircraft since 1985.[270] Iran launched strikes against the Al Udeid Air Base,[271] and Aramco's Ras Tanura oil refining facility.[272] The US ordered the evacuation of non-essential workers in Cyprus in anticipation of Iranian strikes.[273][274] A ballistic missile launched from Iran was intercepted by NATO air defense systems as it entered Turkish airspace, marking an escalation in the conflict.[275] Turkey asserted its right to self-defense after the missile landed in Dörtyol, Hatay Province,[276] and NATO secretary general Mark Rutte stated that the alliance was committed to defending Turkey.[277]

An Iranian frigate, IRIS Dena, was sunk in the Indian Ocean by United States Navy submarine USS Charlotte, about 40 nautical miles (74 km; 46 mi) south of Galle, Sri Lanka. The vessel was returning to Iran following its participation in the International Fleet Review 2026 and the multilateral Exercise MILAN at Visakhapatnam, India.[278][279] The exercise required ships not to carry ammunition, and the US likely knew the Dena was defenseless, since it sent a maritime patrol aircraft to participate.[280] It was the first ship sunk by a submarine in active combat since the Falklands War, and the first by an American submarine since World War II.[ak][283] 104 Iranians were killed.[284]

The government of Azerbaijan said on 5 March that drones from Iran struck Azerbaijan's Nakhchivan exclave[285] damaging an airport and injuring two civilians.[286] Keir Starmer confirmed UK's bases on Cyprus would be used to defend the airspace of Jordan from Iranian drones,[287][288] while Italy, the Netherlands and Spain confirmed they would send warships to defend Cyprus.[289][290][291] Ireland stated it was willing to protect Cyprus and join the European defense coalition mobilized around the island if requested.[292] The IDF killed Hamas official Wassim Attallah al-Ali in Beddawi, Lebanon.[293] Trump said on 6 March that there are "no time limits" for how long the war will continue.[294][295] The Iranian tanker IRIS Bushehr was interned by the Sri Lanka Navy, marking the first instance of a warship being interned in a neutral country since World War II.[296]

On 7 March, the US sent a third aircraft carrier, USS George H. W. Bush, to the Middle East.[297][298][299] The British aircraft carrier HMS Prince of Wales was placed on advanced readiness to defend British interests in the region.[300] On 7 March, Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian apologized for strikes on neighboring countries, citing "miscommunication in the ranks. He stated those countries would not be targeted unless the US launched attacks from them;[301][302] however, Iranian attacks continued, highlighting limited control over the IRGC chief Ahmad Vahidi.[303][304][302]

On 8 March, Khamenei's second son, Mojtaba, was designated as Iran's new supreme leader.[174] US Central Command posted a message on X which urged "civilians in Iran to stay at home" and alleged that "[t]he Iranian regime is knowingly endangering innocent lives by using heavily populated civilian areas to conduct military operations, including launching one-way attack drones and ballistic missiles".[305]

Israeli airstrikes hit Iranian oil storage facilities, killing four people.[306] Strikes on fuel depots near Tehran caused a "river of fire" to pour out along the streets,[307] and the city became engulfed in thick black smoke, causing toxic acidic rain to fall in the surrounding area.[308] Residents were advised by Iranian authorities to stay indoors, wear masks when outside, and conserve food and fuel.[309] Kuwait reported that two of its officers were killed.[310][311] The Saudi Civil Defense agency said that a strike on a compound in Al-Kharj killed two people.[312] US Central Command announced the death of a seventh US service member from an Iranian attack.[313]

The UK confirmed its forces had intercepted an Iranian drone headed towards Iraq, and declared its intention to send a Merlin helicopter to the region to detect aerial threats.[314] According to the Iranian Red Crescent Society, 65 schools and 32 medical facilities had been targeted, and more than 10,000 civilian sites damaged.[315] On 9 March, NATO confirmed the interception of a second ballistic missile in Turkish airspace.[316][317] Turkey deployed six F-16s and air defence systems to Northern Cyprus.[318]

Trump claimed that "the war is very complete, pretty much", after speaking with Russian president Putin,[319] and said "we already won the war in many ways."[320] He claimed that the Strait of Hormuz was open and expressed interest in taking it over from Iran.[321] Trump went back on some comments during a press conference later that day, supporting Defense Secretary Hegseth in stating that the war was just the "beginning of building a new country" and it would end "soon".[322] Following Syrian president Ahmed al-Sharaa's support for the Lebanon's objective to disarm Hezbollah,[323] the group targeted the city of Inkhil in Syria.[324] About a dozen B-1B bombers arrived at bases in Europe.[325]

GPS jamming of uncertain origin disrupted navigation of ships near the Strait of Hormuz.[327] The United States Department of State[328] designated the Muslim Brotherhood branch in Sudan as a terrorist organization.[329][330] On 10 March, an IRGC commander stated that Iran was only firing missiles with payloads of 1,000 kg or more.[331] AFP reported that Iran's attacks were the "most intense and heaviest" since the start of the war.[332] This showed a shift in tactics from saturating air defences to high-impact penetration strikes.[331] American general Dan Caine acknowledged that Iran was fighting back, but not harder than the US expected.[333]

Following the Syrian presidency's support for the disarmament of Hezbollah and a campaign of mobilization by the Syrian army on the Lebanese border,[323][334] shells from Lebanon landed in Serghaya, 20 km (12 mi) from Damascus where the Syrian Armed Forces forces presided.[335] Israel issued an urgent evacuation notice to southern suburbs of Beirut.[336]

Defense analyst AJ Jaff reported that Iran's ballistic missile launch rate fell 92% from day one of the war (480 to 40) and the drone launch rate fell 92% (720 to 60).[337] On 11 March 14 US bombers were deployed to RAF Fairford in the UK, where bombs were being prepared for loading. This followed US war secretary Hegseth's statement that it was the "most intense day of strikes inside Iran".[338]

Israel reportedly struck the Parchin military complex.[339][340][341] A branch of Bank Sepah in Tehran was hit by a strike, prompting the IRGC to warn that they could retaliate by striking US or Israeli banks in the region.[342] Iran hit Stryker, a US-based medical supply company with a cyberattack.[343] On 12 March, UNICEF reported that 300 children had been killed, thousands injured, hundreds of thousands displaced, and millions unable to attend schools due to the war.[344]

Iranian deputy intelligence minister Akbar Ghaffari was killed in an airstrike.[345] An Iranian attack set two tankers on fire off the Iraqi coast, killing one person.[346] The historical Safavid-era building of Rashk-e Jenan, was destroyed by US-Israeli strikes.[347] Other buildings damaged included the Chehel Sotoun pavilion, Rakib Khaneh Mansion, Timurid Hall, Ashraf Hall and the Ali Qapu palace.[348] Many affected buildings and monuments were legally protected by the Blue Shield International,[349] which called damaging them a war crime.[350] French soldiers were injured in a drone strike at a base in Iraqi Kurdistan. French president Emmanuel Macron announced on 13 March that a soldier was killed in the attack.[351]

On 13 March, to help deal with the economic costs of the war, the US temporarily lifted restrictions on the sale of Russian oil.[352] Iran announced a coordinated offensive by its navy, army, and Hezbollah against Israel and US bases.[353] Israel reported that 58 people have been hospitalized due to injuries following a missile strike.[352] Kuwait authorities stated that defense equipment and the country's main airport were attacked, and power lines gone out of service.[354] Missiles entered Turkish air space and were intercepted, with explosions heard near Adana.[355] Israel struck IRGC checkpoints after receiving tip-offs by on the ground informants. Reuters reported Israel had struck positions of the Basij used to suppress Iranian protests.[356]

As of the third week, analysts found little evidence of significant defections in the Iranian military,[al] which have been considered a necessary condition for regime change.[366] The US conducted an attack on Kharg Island, a key oil export hub home to 90 percent of Iran's oil exports. Over 90 military sites were targeted while the oil infrastructure was not targeted "for reasons of decency", according to Trump.[367][368] On 14 March, Kata'ib Hezbollah security commander Abu Ali al-Askari was killed in an airstrike in Baghdad.[369]

The Royal Tulip Al Rasheed Hotel in Baghdad's Green Zone was hit by a drone whilst hosting an EU and Saudi Arabian delegation. The attack was not claimed by anyone; however, due to the proximity of a similar attack 48 hours earlier on the US embassy in Baghdad, there were suspicions it was an Iranian attack.[370]

On 16 March, China and US-aligned NATO nations in Europe rejected Trump's call to provide military support to reopen the Strait of Hormuz.[371][372] Trump rebuked his NATO allies, calling their decision a "very foolish mistake".[373] On the same day, White House Press Secretary Karoline Leavitt stated that the Trump administration will not rule out a military draft for the war. While doing so, she clarified that a draft is not "part of the current plan," but that the president is open to any suggestions.[374] On 17 March, Trump made a statement on Truth Social renouncing NATO's assistance, and unexpectedly, US allies in the Indo-Pacific, namely Japan, South Korea, and Australia, for refusing to join US-led attacks on Iran during the war.[375][376][377][378] Trump declared that the United States "[does] not need the help of anyone" regarding the war.[379]

In the morning of 17 March, senior Iranian officials, including Ali Larijani and Basij chief Gholamreza Soleimani were targeted by Israeli airstrikes.[380][381] Both their deaths were later confirmed by Iranian state media.[382] In response, Iran launched a missile barrage that killed two Israeli civilians in Ramat Gan.[383] The same day, Israel launched a ground invasion of southern Lebanon.[384]

On 18 March,[385] Israel struck the South Pars natural gas field in the Persian Gulf and its neighboring refineries in Iran with US coordination.[386] In retaliation, Iran attacked the world's largest LNG production facility in Qatar. Trump claimed he was unaware of the South Pars attack, promised that there would be no more Israeli attacks on Iranian oil infrastructure, and threatened Iran not to continue attacking Qatari energy infrastructure.[385][387] Israel said it had killed Iranian intelligence minister Esmaeil Khatib in an overnight airstrike.[388] Pezeshkian confirmed Khatib's killing.[389] A hair salon in Beit Awwa was struck by a projectile, killing four women,[390] with Israeli authorities stating that it was most likely cluster munitions and Palestinian authorities saying it was an errant Israeli interceptor.[391][392]

On 19 March, a US F-35 made an emergency landing after a suspected hit by Iranian forces.[393][394] A BAZAN Group refinery in Haifa was hit during a broader Iranian missile attack on the area as a retaliation for Israeli attacks on South Pars gas facilities.[395][396] Netanyahu insisted that "You can't make a revolution from the air" and that "there must be a ground component—I won't share with you all the options", implying that there was a potential for limited assault operations involving soldiers on the ground in Iran.[397] The US began an aerial campaign against Iranian vessels and drones in the Strait of Hormuz in an effort to reopen it to international shipping.[398]

Admiral Brad Cooper said that the US military had so far struck more than 8,000 Iranian military targets, including 130 vessels.[399] On 21 March, the US conducted strikes on the Natanz Nuclear Facility using bunker buster bombs to target the site.[400] Russia condemned the strikes on Natanz as a "blatant violation of international law," while the IAEA urged military restraint "to avoid any risk of a nuclear accident".[401] In response, Iran struck the southern Israeli town of Dimona, injuring at least 78 people.[402] Iran said that it targeted the Shimon Peres Negev Nuclear Research Center.[403][404]

Citing unnamed US officials, CNN and The Wall Street Journal reported that Iran unsuccessfully attempted to strike the joint US–UK military base at Diego Garcia on the Chagos Islands in the British Indian Ocean Territory.[405] The report said one of the missiles broke apart mid-flight, while another was intercepted by a SM-3 air defence missile launched by a US warship.[406] Israel said that Iran used a two-stage intercontinental ballistic missile to target the island.[407][408] Iran denied launching missiles towards Diego Garcia, saying that it was an Israeli false flag attack.[409] In response the UK Foreign Secretary confirmed and denounced the Iranian attack on their end, and additionally expanded permission for the United States to bomb certain targets using their bases.[410][411] No evidence has been presented that the alleged Iranian missiles neared Diego Garcia or that one was intercepted.[412]

The Houthi movement in Yemen warned that it would respond to any escalation against Iran, including efforts to reopen the Strait of Hormuz. It specifically warned the two Arab countries offering to join the Strait of Hormuz campaign—Bahrain and the United Arab Emirates—that they "will be the first to lose in this battle".[413] The Houthis further threatened to join the war in the event that US allies joined the attack on Iran or if the US and Israel used the Red Sea to carry out operations.[414] Lebanon's government expelled the Iranian ambassador.[415]

Trump issued an ultimatum to Iran, threatening to strike its power plants unless it opened the Strait of Hormuz within 48 hours.[416] Iran doubled down, threatening to "completely" close the Strait of Hormuz and strike vital infrastructure across the region such as energy and desalination facilities critical for drinking water.[417] Iranian opposition figure and former crown prince Reza Pahlavi called on Trump and Netanyahu to target the military while sparing civilian infrastructure which "Iranians will need to rebuild our country."[418] Halfway through the deadline, Trump announced that he was postponing strikes against Iranian power plants for five days,[419] and said the US was negotiating with Iran to end the war.[420] Iran denied the talks ever took place or were taking place and called the president "deceitful".[421] Iran rejected the 15-point peace plan presented by the US.[422][423] Iran asserted that Lebanon must be included as part of a ceasefire deal, thereby making a ceasefire conditional on an end to the 2026 Lebanon war against Hezbollah.[424]

On 24 March, Israel or its allies shot down an Iranian missile crossing above Lebanon at high altitude, according to the Lebanese army, which also confirmed that the missile was not targeting Lebanon. This was the first time during the current conflict when a shootdown of an Iranian missile took place over Lebanese territory.[425][426]

A US strike on the Habbaniya military base—which hosts units from the Popular Mobilization Forces—in Al Anbar Governorate killed seven members of the Iraqi Armed Forces and injured 13 others. In response, Iraqi prime minister Mohammed Shia' al-Sudani summoned the US embassy's chargé d'affaires in Baghdad.[427] Iranian state media threatened that Iran could seize Bahraini and Emirati territory if the US "makes any mistakes", while signaling its readiness to open a new front in Yemen by closing the Bab al-Mandab Strait together with the Houthis.[428][429] Israel said it killed Iran's top naval commander, Alireza Tangsiri, purportedly as part of an effort to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Katz said Tangsiri was "directly responsible" for the closure of.[430][431][432]

On 27 March, a day after Trump and Hegseth announced the "neutralization" of Iran's military, an Iranian missile and drone strike on Prince Sultan Air Base damaged several US refueling aircraft and injured at least 15 US soldiers. Despite Iran's seizure of two cargo ships,[543] Trump claimed total control over the strait.[544] The Guardian described the situation as a "dual blockade", saying that while the US Navy could blockade Iranian ports, it had been unable to stop Iran's blockade and open the strait to allies.[543] Israel and Lebanon agreed a three-week extension of their ceasefire.[545]

On 8 June, the IDF announced that it struck military sites in Iran, with explosions reported in Tehran, Isfahan, and Tabriz.[546] This triggered an exchange between the two countries.[547] Two Iranian soldiers were killed in an Israeli attack.[548] Iran afterwards said it had ceased military actions against Israel.[549] Israel stopped strikes at Trump's request.[550]

Trump said he had authorized the lifting of the US blockade.[560] On 15 June, US vice president JD Vance announced that the memorandum was digitally signed by both countries the previous day.[561] On 17 June, Trump and Iranian president Masoud Pezeshkian signed the memorandum of understanding to end the war, with Trump signing it during dinner with French president Emmanuel Macron at the Palace of Versailles after the G7 summit.[562] On 18 June, Pakistan stated that the signing of the memorandum implies Tehran will reopen the Hormuz "instantly" and the American blockade will end "immediately."[563] CENTCOM announced that it had removed the naval blockade.[564]

On 19 June, Trump announced a renewed ceasefire between Israel and Hezbollah in the 2026 Lebanon war, facilitated by the US, Qatar, and Iran.[565][566] Hezbollah announced an attack on Israeli forces trying to capture Ali al-Taher in Nabatieh.[567] Israel continued to strike southern Lebanon numerous times.[568]

The administrative council of the International Maritime Organization (IMO) agreed that member states should reject Iranian efforts to ‌impose sovereignty over the Hormuz and Tehran's "unilateral decision" to form a body to control traffic on the waterway.[579] The IRGC's navy said it closed the strait until further notice after firing a warning shot at a vessel trying to transit through an unapproved route.[580] On 13 July, Trump announced that the US will reinstate the "Iranian blockade in the Strait" and impose a 20% toll on cargo shipping through it.[581] The Yemeni government and Saudi Arabia struck the Sanaa International Airport controlled by the Houthis,[582][583] allegedly to prevent an Iranian plane from landing.[584] The Houthis retaliated by launching missiles and drones against Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport.[585][586] The Combined Maritime Forces' Joint Maritime Information Centre (JMIC), led by America, announced that the US blockade on Iran would start the following day.[587] The US announced that it hit military targets throughout Iran including Bushehr, Chabahar, Jask, Konarak, Abu Musa, and Bandar Abbas.[am][590] Two Emirati tankers were reportedly struck by Iranian cruise missiles in the strait in Oman's territorial waters, killing one Indian crew member and injuring two critically.[591][592] On 14 July, Trump cancelled plans to impose fees in the strait.[593] The IMO said that the death toll from Hormuz ship attacks on that day increased to two.[594]

On 20 July, the Houthis declared a blockade of Saudi Arabian ports and ships in the Bab-el-Mandeb,[595] a strait connecting the Red Sea to the Indian Ocean.

On 21 July, the British military stated that a tanker reported being hit by an unknown projectile in the Hormuz eight nautical miles northeast of Limah in Oman.[596]

On 23 July, the Shalamcheh crossing on the Iran-Iraq border was hit while being used by Iranian pilgrims ahead of Arbaeen.[597] Iran's semi-official media and state media reported that two people including a soldier were killed and 11 others were wounded in the American attack.[598][599] In response, the IRGC claimed attacking Ali Al Salem Air Base and Camp Udairi, while the Iranian Army said it hit Camp Doha, Ali Al Salem and Camp Arifjan.[600] A B-1 long-range bomber was used by the US to strike IRGC targets in Iran for the first time since fighting with Iran resumed 12 days prior.[601] The New York Times reported that Iran rejected a US cease-fire plan provided by Iraqi prime minister Ali al-Zaidi, stating that their government was not interested in a temporary agreement that left the subject of control over the Hormuz unresolved.[602] Iran later publicly confirmed its stance.[603]

On 24 July, the US concluded its 13th consecutive evening of strikes in Iran.[604][605] In response to the alleged US attacks on Darkhovin Nuclear Power Plant, the IRGC claimed setting fire to three depots in Udeiri Camp, damaging the communications tower of the US naval base in Bahrain, and destroying the last intact building of Amazon's data center in the country.[606] The Iranian Army reported targeting US deployments in the Isa Air Base in Bahrain and Azraq Air Base in Jordan.[606] The Wall Street Journal reported, citing sources familiar with the subject that Bahrain and Kuwait discreetly struck Iran earlier in the month, with intelligence and defensive air cover from the UAE.[10]

On 25 July, US forces ceased overnight strikes against Iran after 13 nights of attacks. President Trump reportedly paused plans for further escalation, citing depleted Pentagon stocks of regional air defence munitions, particularly Patriot antimissile interceptors, and a recommendation from CENTCOM commander Admiral Brad Cooper to halt the Hormuz campaign unless the US was prepared to escalate.[607][608]

Jordan declared that they shot down five missiles from Iran. [632][633] Kuwait stated that it downed Iranian drones which targeted a government facility and a private company.[634] The New York Times reported, citing state and local officials, that evidence leads to Iran in a series of cyberattacks against water systems in at least seven US states, with Michigan being the second state to report the attacks publicly.[635]
